check_search_quota.description: See how many searches are left before spending one. Asking costs nothing against the quota, so put it in front of a batch: a run that would stop halfway through can decide not to start. Also reports how many searches may run at once and, optionally, a breakdown of recent usage. No API key required.
check_search_quota.name: check_search_quota

parameters.description: Also return a breakdown of recent requests by outcome. Leave empty for the quota alone.
parameters.name: period

concurrency.description: How many searches may run at once. Sending more than this at a time fails the extras.

history.description: Requests per period, by outcome. Empty unless a period was asked for.

bad_request.description: How many were rejected as malformed.

quota_or_concurrency.description: How many were refused for quota or for running too many at once.

server_error.description: How many failed on their side.

unavailable.description: How many found the queue full or the database unavailable.

id.description: Who trace.moe counted this against: an email address for a key, or an IP address for a guest.

is_depleted.description: Whether the quota is spent, so the next search would fail.

period.description: The history period asked for, if any.

priority.description: Where searches sit in the queue when trace.moe is busy. 0 is the lowest.

quota.description: Searches allowed in a rolling 24 hours.

quota_used_percent.description: How much of the quota is gone.

using_api_key.description: Whether this connection sent an api key. Without one the quota belongs to the server's IP address and is shared with anything else using it.

check_service_status.description: Check whether trace.moe is answering, how quickly, and how much anime it currently has indexed. This is the one action that reports a problem as a value instead of failing the step, so a scheduled workflow can tell an outage from an empty answer. Being asked to slow down is reported separately from being down. No API key required.
check_service_status.name: check_service_status

index_rows.description: How many vectors the search index holds. Normally tracks the frame count.

index_updated.description: When the index was last rebuilt.

indexed_duration_hours.description: How many hours of anime that comes to.

indexed_files.description: How many video files are indexed.

indexed_frames.description: How many frames are searchable across them.

online.description: Whether trace.moe answered with a usable report of its index.

rate_limited.description: Whether it asked this workspace to slow down.

reachable.description: Whether it answered at all. Reachable but not online means it is refusing rather than down.

response_time_ms.description: How long the answer took, in milliseconds.

status_code.description: The HTTP status it answered with, or empty when it could not be reached.

using_api_key.description: Whether this connection sent an api key.

find_scene_in_anime.description: Answer 'which episode is this from?' when the show is already known: search only inside one anime, named by title or by AniList id. Restricting the search is what makes the similarity meaningful, because the answer is the closest frame in that show rather than the closest frame in every show. A title is looked up first, and the anime that was settled on comes back with the match. No API key required.
find_scene_in_anime.display_name: Find a scene in one anime
find_scene_in_anime.name: find_scene_in_anime

parameters.description: The frame to identify: upload a screenshot, use a file from an earlier step, or paste a public link to one. A video or a GIF works too - trace.moe reads the first frame. 640x360 is plenty; a larger image does not search any better, and anything over 25MB is refused.
parameters.name: image

parameters.description: Which anime to search inside: a title, a synonym, or an AniList id if you have one. A title is resolved through trace.moe's own anime lookup, so a near miss usually still finds the right show.

description: Identify anime from a screenshot with trace.moe, the anime scene search engine. Give it a frame and it names the show, the episode and the second it appears, with a still and a clip of the scene. Search everything indexed, or search inside one anime when you know the show but not the episode, and look a title up to get its AniList and MyAnimeList ids. Because the service always answers with its closest frames even when none is right, every search says how confident the match is so a workflow can act on a real one and stop at a coincidence. Previews can be saved as files before their links expire, and the remaining search quota can be checked without spending any of it. Works with no API key; adding one from a sponsor account raises the daily limit.
